title: Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation
abstract: Spatial gene expression results from the superposition of multiple sources of variation in gene expression across different spatial scales, including local microenvironment-associated variation and global spatial gradients. Spatial foundation models (SFMs) are large-scale machine learning models trained on cohorts of spatial transcriptomics (ST) data that, in principle, learn the different sources of spatial variation in gene expression. However, the embeddings learned by SFMs are difficult to interpret, and it remains unclear whether they fully capture such spatial variation. Here, we develop SAFFRON, a sparse autoencoder (SAE)-based framework for interpreting and evaluating SFMs. SAFFRON uses a Matryoshka SAE to decompose dense SFM embeddings into sparse, human-interpretable features and evaluates whether these features correlate with known sources of spatial variation. Using SAFFRON, we systematically benchmark the ability of several recent SFMs to identify local and global spatial variation in gene expression. We find that only two SFMs learn global spatial gradients more accurately than naive, non-foundation model baselines; further investigating one such SFM, SAFFRON reveals that these gradients are concentrated in a small subset of sparse, human-interpretable SAE features. On the other hand, no SFM learns local patterns (A{beta} plaque microenvironment-associated patterns) more accurately than such baselines. Our findings suggest that current SFMs do not systematically learn multi-scale spatial variation in gene expression. Code: SAFFRON is available at https://github.com/chitra-lab/SAFFRON.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出基于Matryoshka稀疏自编码器（SAE）的SAFFRON框架，将空间基础模型（SFM）的稠密嵌入分解为可解释的稀疏特征，并用其系统评估SFM对局部（Aβ斑块微环境）与全局空间梯度变化的捕获能力。
llm.summary_zh: 本文提出SAFFRON，一个基于Matryoshka稀疏自编码器的框架，用于解释和评估空间转录组基础模型（SFM）的嵌入，将稠密嵌入分解为可解释的稀疏特征，并检验其是否与已知的空间变异来源相关。基准测试显示，只有两个SFM在全局空间梯度上优于非基础模型基线，且相关梯度集中在少数稀疏特征中；而没有任何SFM在局部Aβ斑块微环境模式上优于基线。结论是当前SFM并未系统地学习多尺度空间基因表达变异。

title: Cross-attention and language models reveal the interpretability of functional predictions for the human olfactory receptor family
abstract: The attention mechanism offers a route to data-driven discovery of biological principles. However, for important protein families such as human olfactory receptors, the extent to which attention can associate with biologically meaningful key regions lacks systematic validation. In this study, using human olfactory receptors (ORs) as a model, we constructed CrossVOI, a VOC-OR interaction prediction framework based on protein language models and cross-attention. Based on this architecture, we systematically analyzed the attention distributions of CrossVOI and found that although site-level attention for individual ORs was not stably reproducible, the averaged attention consistently concentrated on the C-terminal region and non-conserved sequence regions. In addition, we quantified the allocation of attention on ORs and VOCs and, combined with ablation experiments, explored the effects of data representation and model architectural complexity on the OR-VOC interaction prediction task. The results showed that increasing representation and model complexity did not always improve model performance on the prediction task. In summary, we propose CrossVOI, an interpretable OR-VOC interaction prediction framework with predictive performance comparable to that of current state-of-the-art models, and analyze the interpretability of the attention mechanism for human ORs. This study provides insights into the interpretability of protein function prediction methods and may help clarify the biological relevance of attention, and may guide future experimental validation.

llm.novelty_zh: 用蛋白语言模型加交叉注意力预测人类嗅觉受体与挥发性有机化合物的相互作用，并系统检验注意力权重是否对应生物学上关键的区域。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究提出 CrossVOI 框架，基于蛋白语言模型和交叉注意力预测人类嗅觉受体（OR）与挥发性有机化合物（VOC）的相互作用，性能与现有先进模型相当。作者分析了注意力分布，发现平均注意力集中于 C 端区域和非保守序列区，但单位点注意力可重复性较差，并通过消融实验表明增加表征和模型复杂度不一定提升性能。该工作与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型的主题关系很弱，主要属于受体-配体功能预测与可解释性范畴。

title: Lacuna: Cryptic Binding Pocket Discovery via Conformational Ensemble Analysis
abstract: Lacuna, an open-source Python tool for discovering cryptic binding pockets: sites that are absent or too small to detect in the unbound structure of a protein, RNA or DNA and open only during conformational fluctuation. Most binding-site predictors score a single static structure, the very structure in which a cryptic site is invisible. Lacuna generates a conformational ensemble from any input structure, detects pockets independently in every conformer, clusters the detections into persistent sites, and ranks those sites with a model fitted on within-structure pairs. Ensemble generation is pluggable: normal mode analysis (NMA) by default, with implicit-solvent molecular dynamics, Boltz-2 diffusion sampling or a user-supplied ensemble as alternatives. On the designated test fold of CryptoBench, all 222 structures of which are scored, the zero-dependency default recovers the cryptic site for 59.9% of structures in its top five predictions, and it recovers 69% on the PocketMiner set, 41% on a curated set of literature apo/holo pairs and 89% of structures in the already-open COACH420 set. On that test fold, ordering the candidate set with the fitted ranker rather than the analytic rule it replaced accounts for a gain of 27.5 points (95% CI +21.2 to +33.8), the largest single effect measured here. An optional protein-language-model (PLM) ranker reaches 66.1% on a 180-structure subset of that fold, and pooling the geometric detector with an optional learned surface detector raises top-five recovery to 73.9% and the fraction of structures in which the site is found at all to 86.4% in a separate held-out evaluation at five conformers (184 structures; both optional configurations measured with version 1.4.0). A new per-residue cryptic-site propensity reaches AUROC 0.766 and AUPRC 0.340 on the same test fold (231 targets), against 0.249 for the same scorer on the input structure alone, so the ensemble carries information the input does not. RNA and DNA need no extra flags; on RNA sites with no cavity in the input the ensemble raises the fraction found from 44% to 73% (measured with version 1.3.0). With the default NMA backend the pocket report is identical at any thread count and between Windows and Linux on the 40 proteins compared, ensemble generation needs less than half the memory of version 1.4.0 from 1,300 residues up, and the full pipeline is 7% to 30% faster than 1.4.0 on the reference proteins of the repository's speed table. At the default 20 conformers it takes a median of 1.9 seconds per chain on one CPU thread (30 chains of 57 to 676 residues). Outputs include docking-ready Boltz constraints and AutoDock Vina boxes, a per-residue propensity map and the conformer ensemble. Lacuna is MIT licensed, available at https://github.com/mooreneural/lacuna and on PyPI as lacuna-pockets, and runs as a local MCP server for AI assistants and on hosted no-install platforms.
